definitions.gloss: picking up and dropping off; transportation to and from
definitions.explanation: The act of taking someone to a destination and bringing them back, or more broadly, providing rides both ways. Very common in the context of children, elderly care, and daily commuting.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{送|おく}り{迎|むか}えをする。
examples.english: To pick up and drop off the children.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{学校|がっこう}への{送|おく}り{迎|むか}えが{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: The daily school run is exhausting.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}まで{車|くるま}で{送|おく}り{迎|むか}えしてくれる{人|ひと}がいると{助|たす}かる。
examples.english: It would be a great help to have someone who can drive me to and from the station.

notes:
USAGE:
{送|おく}り{迎|むか}え combines {送|おく}り (sending/taking someone) and {迎|むか}え (picking up/meeting someone) into one word meaning round-trip transportation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- の{送|おく}り{迎|むか}えをする (to do the pickup and drop-off for...)
- への{送|おく}り{迎|むか}え (transportation to and from...)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {子|こ}どもの{送|おく}り{迎|むか}え (school run for children)
- {送|おく}り{迎|むか}えバス (shuttle bus)
- {送|おく}り{迎|むか}えサービス (pickup and drop-off service)

This word is especially common among parents discussing daily routines with childcare and school.
